claims.text: A blog post titled 'SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi' exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/ and covers the engine mechanics behind SST's migration to Pulumi.
AWS CDK tied infrastructure to AWS, debugging was frustrating due to CloudFormation templates, and multi-cloud was nearly impossible.
SST was originally built on AWS CDK, which allowed developers to define infrastructure using TypeScript or Python.
AWS CDK is AWS-only, while Pulumi supports AWS, Azure, GCP, and on-prem; Pulumi deploys faster than CDK; CDK secrets management is AWS Secrets Manager only.
SST Ion is the code name for a new engine deploying SST applications using Pulumi instead of CDK and CloudFormation; once stable it will be released as SST v3.
SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for its providers and deployment engine and bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.
Pulumi supports defining infrastructure in TypeScript, Python, Go, or C# and deploying to AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and on-premises.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make the underlying cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` requires no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account or Pulumi Cloud dependency; the engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST keeps its state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account rather than in Pulumi Cloud.
SST v3 is the Ion-based rewrite of SST.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack.
SST can deploy to AWS and more than 150 other providers.
SST apps define infrastructure and code together in a single `sst.config.ts` file, and `sst deploy` handles provisioning end to end.
Through 2023, SST's provisioning layer was built directly on AWS CDK and CloudFormation.
In late 2023 the SST team began a rewrite code-named Ion that replaced the entire deployment layer.
Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.
The SST team has repeatedly said about their own architecture that SST is built on the Pulumi engine since the rewrite shipped.

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: 'Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN).'

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: 'When you run `sst deploy`, those resources make a call to an embedded Pulumi engine that makes a call to their bridged Terraform provider, and this makes the AWS SDK calls to create your resources.'
The SST docs 'What is SST' say: 'SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for the providers and the deployment engine. And Terraform's providers are bridged through Pulumi.'
Gautier Blandin's article 'Terraform, Pulumi, SST: a tradeoff analysis' says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST's constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka's dev.to article says: 'You may notice right away the imports from Pulumi. It means the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi now.'
The published package.json for SST's platform package depends on @pulumi/pulumi, first-party Pulumi providers for AWS, Cloudflare, Docker builds and more, and the Pulumiverse Vercel provider.

The SST repository is at anomalyco/sst (formerly sst/sst), and its platform/package.json lists @pulumi/pulumi, @pulumi/aws, @pulumi/cloudflare, @pulumi/command, @pulumi/docker-build, @pulumi/random, @pulumi/tls, and @pulumiverse/vercel as direct dependencies.
The Pulumi engine diffs desired vs. actual state, builds a dependency graph, and orders operations.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge (pulumi-terraform-bridge) translates Terraform provider resources into cloud API calls for the Pulumi engine.
Pulumi's engine provides plumbing to hundreds of provider APIs.
AWS alone exposes hundreds of resource types.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge was built specifically to let projects like SST reuse Terraform's provider ecosystem.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, a network call to Pulumi Cloud, or any Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API lets teams embed Pulumi programs inside their own tools.
The Terraform provider bridge lets any Pulumi user consume Terraform providers directly.
Nitric and Defang also run application deployments through the Pulumi engine.
Nitric's docs state that 'all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments'.
Official Nitric providers are built directly on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Nitric is a cloud-agnostic application framework.
Defang deploys Docker Compose applications to the cloud, and its Pulumi provider is described as taking 'a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`'.
Most SST users never write Pulumi code and work entirely in SST's component model.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly in Pulumi and deployed as part of the same SST app.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The `sst` npm package had roughly 796,000 (796,291) weekly downloads for the week of September 5-11, 2026.
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent.
opencode has a larger following on GitHub than SST.
SST does not invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
The opencode work has not changed SST's release cadence or its dependency on the Pulumi engine.

Pulumi Cloud provides cross-team visibility into infrastructure state, policy as code provides centrally enforced guardrails, and components allow sharing infrastructure patterns across an organization.
SST doesn't expose cross-team visibility, policy enforcement, or infrastructure shared across more than one application on its own.
The linked pages exist: /blog/aws-cdk-vs-pulumi-why-sst-switched/, /docs/iac/guides/basics/how-pulumi-works/, /blog/any-terraform-provider/, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
